title: Frank Tiberi: ten years in the band and his complex tenor playing
summary: Tiberi has been with Herman ten years and brought in Gregory Herbert; Herman admits he often cannot follow Tiberi's complex tenor playing.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: There's two guys I just want to talk about because they've been with you so long, now. And one is Frank Tiberi. What is it, one decade about now, isn't it?
Ten years, geez. He's contributed an awful lot.
Yeah, I think one of his big contributions was bringing into the band Gregory Herbert.
He was -- to my knowledge, Gregory Herbert was his discovery. They worked together in Atlantic City.
Right, right, yeah. They were friends
Yeah. And I'll confess with no qualms at all that for the first couple of years I couldn't understand Frank's tenor playing at all. And after ten years, I'm not sure I do all the time.
And he's very inventive in his fashion. He's a guy who's not a boy, and he's lived for a long time, as I have.
And there are as many things that are strictly Frank's, just as I'm sure I have that are strictly my own.
Yeah. A lot of his playing is extremely complex, but it's deceiving. It comes across very simple, and that's very hard to pull off. Seems to me he communicates.
That's right. Well, he knows what he wants, and that's what he's doing. And he doesn't really pay that much attention to whether he's conforming to the realm of old arranging.
